notes:
Kansas has no recurring franchise-type levy on a default LLC: applies is false. The Department of Revenue's franchise tax page states in terms that there is no Kansas franchise tax for tax year 2011 and after, and explains the pre-2011 tax and its rate schedule as history. The only remaining privilege tax is an income tax paid by financial institutions, and the corporate income tax under K.S.A. 79-32,110(c) is imposed on every corporation doing business in Kansas, not on a default LLC.
collectedWithAnnualReport is null: no franchise-type levy exists, and root states.json carries annual_report_fee 53 for Kansas, the Secretary of State's annual report filing fee - a separate payment with no tax to overlap. The pre-2011 franchise-tax page notes the old combined franchise tax and Secretary of State filing fee were due with the annual report; the franchise tax half no longer exists.
stateIncomeTax: a default LLC is a flow-through entity under Kansas law: the Department's Small Business/Sub-S page says S corporations are generally exempt from tax and each shareholder includes the income on his or her income tax return, and partnerships and LLCs file Form K-120S. Individual income tax rates for tax year 2024 and later are 5.2% up to the bracket threshold and 5.58% above it (K.S.A. 79-32,110(a)(1)(B)); the 2025 K-40 booklet confirms the same two rates.
hasPTETElection is true: the SALT Parity Act allows electing pass-through entities to pay Kansas income tax at the entity level, and the 2025 K-120S instructions provide the election and compute the electing pass-through entity income tax at 5.58% of the electing partners' taxable income, with members claiming the Kansas Tax @ 5.58% credit on Form K-40.
